research_updates.title: Investment audit — plans, permits, lease accounting and cash kept separate
research_updates.notes: Source families searched: Equinix newsroom and investor filings; SEC EDGAR 8-K/10-Q/10-K exhibits and XBRL facts; Digital Realty 2011-2026 filings; Clise and DLR property materials; Seattle Services Portal attachments; City Open Data Building Permits dataset 76t5-zqzr; and contractor profiles. Searches used Equinix SE3, Switch & Data WA One LLC, 2020 Fifth Avenue, parcel 0659000905, $60 million, capex, contribution, investment, asset, acquisition, lease, rent, financing and cost across 2010-2026. Digital Realty's 2011 filing resolves approximately $4.1 million of funded cash for its 50% ownership/development JV interest against approximately $22.9 million committed; only the funded investor amount is retained as actual. The approximately $60 million operator plan, approximately $110 million lease obligation, $96.707 million 2016 gross building/improvement basis and permit values remain incompatible and are not summed. No total-project cash capex, Equinix equipment ledger, investor roll-forward, annual investment series, construction disbursement or local-retention amount was found.

research_updates.title: Construction audit — original permit scopes and completion dates recovered
research_updates.notes: Seattle Services Portal exact-address search returned 407 records (mixed record types) through 2026. The original records opened were 6229374-CN, 6262351-CN, 3010224-LU and 6336933-SS; the main permit's attachment index spans four pages and its first 25 entries include the certificate of occupancy, special-inspection finals, site photos and preliminary application, but no invoice or payroll. A separate exact Socrata route, data.seattle.gov/resource/76t5-zqzr.json with upper(originaladdress1) like '%2020 5TH%', returned only three building permits: the two retained permits and 6292157-CN, a $307,500 parent skybridge record marked expired/incomplete. Description-reference query '%6292157%' returned four applications: parent 6292157-CN plus completed cross-property children 6294136-CN ($7,500, 2001 Sixth), 6294137-CN ($307,500, 2033 Sixth) and 6294138-CN ($7,500, 2000 Fifth). Those values are not assigned to SE3 or summed because the parent is incomplete and the children span multiple properties. No complete construction cost, payment ledger, peak workforce, worker count, certified payroll, worker residence or non-overlap contract total was found.

source.title: Seattle Services Portal — Construction Permit 6229374-CN
source.publisher: City of Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections
source.notes: The completed permit records the parking-garage-to-data-center change of use, 47,029 square feet of data-center area on levels five through eight and 43,650 square feet of parking from basement through level four. It was issued April 2, 2012, received a certificate of occupancy March 7, 2013, completed inspections March 12, 2013, and reports $8,846,783 total issued value: $8,533,783 new and $313,000 alteration. The portal also reports a $8,481,269 intake valuation, 2009 Seattle Building Code review, substantial-alteration and emergency-system flags, and a renewable-energy-purchase-documentation condition on drawing G005. The attachments index spans four pages; its first 25 entries include the certificate of occupancy, special-inspection reports, site photos and preliminary application, but no invoice, payment ledger or certified payroll. Permit value is administrative valuation, not audited developer spending or supplier payment.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit — identified firms lack payment and locality evidence
research_updates.notes: Sources searched: the AGC/DJC 2014 award archive, Seattle permit contacts and attachments, Clise and Digital Realty pages, contractor case studies, procurement/check-register routes, SEC filings, BLS May 2013 OES and BLS/QCEW archives. Exact searches combined 2020 Fifth, SE3, Equinix, Clise, Digital Realty, Lydig Construction, Sclater Partners, Titan Electric, vendor, subcontractor, invoice, contract, procurement and local spend across 2010-2026. Lydig is identified as general contractor, Sclater as architect, and Titan Electric appears on later tenant electrical permits. The AGC profile reports 50,482 total project worker hours and a $50 million-$100 million private-building award category; BLS Table A supplies a contemporaneous $27.38 Seattle-Bellevue-Everett construction/extraction mean wage. Those inputs support separately labeled construction-value and labor-income sensitivities. Supplier/non-labor residual: reject after explicit subtraction test. The award source does not define whether its category is total project cost, contract value, eligible construction cost, or hard-plus-soft cost, and the hours source does not say it covers all contractors, trades or labor. Therefore category value minus modeled base wages would be an unidentified residual that could include unreported labor, benefits, design, owner costs, overhead, profit and equipment; it cannot be labeled supplier purchases or local retention. No firm-specific payment, complete vendor roster, supplier address at performance, King County share, operating procurement or non-overlap local-spend ledger was found, so no supplier contribution or multiplier passes.

source.title: 2014 AGC Build Washington Awards — 2020 Fifth Avenue Data Center
source.publisher: Seattle Daily Journal of Commerce / Associated General Contractors of Washington
source.notes: The project profile names Clise Properties and Digital Realty as owner/developer, Lydig Construction as general contractor and Sclater Partners as architect. It reports 50,482 total project worker hours, one injury and places the project in the $50 million-$100 million private-building award category, but gives no worker count, payroll, residence, certified hours, contract payment, supplier geography or exact project cost. The category endpoints and midpoint support only a separately labeled construction-value sensitivity; they are not audited spend, a bid, a contract value or a claim that the category is inclusive of every hard and soft cost. The hours separately support the low-confidence wage benchmark. Because the profile does not define category cost coverage or whether the hours cover every contractor and trade, subtracting modeled wages cannot identify materials, suppliers, overhead, profit or local retention.

research_updates.title: Operations audit — operating status and footprint without jobs or payroll
research_updates.notes: Sources searched: Equinix 2013 opening and current SE3 pages, annual reports, facility directories, Seattle permit chronology, job postings, workforce reporting, Washington ESD 2012 occupational estimates and BLS May 2023 OEWS. Queries combined SE3, 2020 Fifth, Seattle IBX, employee, FTE, technician, engineer, security, contractor, shift, payroll, wage, benefits, residence, operating expense, revenue and occupancy across 2013-2026. The opening release expressly establishes 24-hour operations and security and the current page identifies on-site security; 2015-2026 electrical permits show continuing tenant fit-outs. That evidence supports only a strictly conditional one-active-security-post 24x7 coverage floor: 8,760 coverage hours divided by 2,080 paid hours, with 1.00/1.15/1.30 relief-factor sensitivities, plus a separately labeled base-wage cost benchmark using official $17.18 near-opening and $22.79 current regional security-guard means. The release does not state that one post is continuously staffed, and neither model is observed site headcount, payroll, contractor count or total operations staffing. No site FTE, employee/contractor split, simultaneous-post count, actual wage, benefits, worker residence, annual revenue, operating expense, customer occupancy series or turnover was found.

research_updates.title: Public-cost and incentive audit — later urban preference not assigned to SE3
research_updates.notes: Sources searched: Washington JLARC tax-preference reviews and urban-facility tables; Department of Revenue/Commerce preference routes; Seattle Council/Clerk contracts, agendas and Waterfront LID roll CF 322021; assessor exemption fields; SDOT skybridge references; permits; and operator/landlord filings. Queries used Equinix, Switch & Data WA One, SE3, 2020 Fifth, parcel 0659000905, data center, exemption, sales/use tax, incentive, abatement, grant, reimbursement, subsidy, fee, assessment and clawback across 2010-2026. The urban data-center preference began in 2022 and JLARC's Equinix entry opened in 2017, not SE3's 2013 opening; confidentiality prevents treating omission as proof of zero. CF 322021 reports a $40,749.49 Waterfront LID assessment to 2020 Fifth Holdings LLC; the lease's broad general/special-assessment definition makes tenant reimbursement possible, but the garage deduction, payment election and reconciliation remain unavailable. The lease also assigns 50% of the annual skybridge fee to the tenant, but no fee amount or invoice was found. No SE3 award, exemption certificate, abatement, public grant, appropriation, reimbursement or complete net public-cost ledger was found.

research_updates.title: Resource audit — contractual capacity retained; meters and emissions absent
research_updates.notes: Sources searched: executed-lease utility and hazardous-material sections; current and 2013 Seattle City Light tariffs/bill comparisons; EIA Washington industrial-price history; EPA eGRID summary, mapping and Power Profiler guidance; Seattle Services Portal permit details, conditions and attachments; Seattle Public Utilities side-sewer record 6336933-SS; Puget Sound Clean Air construction-permit and Title V pages; Washington Ecology facility/data-center routes; EIA-861/861M; CBECS; and operator sustainability pages. Exact queries combined Equinix, Switch & Data WA One, SE3, 2020 Fifth, building ID 000026949-BD, meter, account, bill, kWh, demand, rate, PUE, water, wastewater, generator, Omntec, diesel, fuel, runtime, air permit, registration and emissions across 2010-2026. The lease's two City Light basement vaults and up-to-9-MW tenant allocation remain a projection, with landlord-paid, submeter-rebilled electricity. Current City Light Large service has distinct City/Downtown schedules and energy, demand, base and power-factor elements; the 2013 official-statement examples, EIA 2013/2024 Washington industrial prices and current Downtown Large peak energy charge support only a broad energy-cost benchmark when paired with the retained throughput sensitivity. EPA's 635.267 lb CO2e/MWh NWPP total-output factor supports only a gross location-based sensitivity. Neither is a bill or measured emissions, and no renewable certificate, utility carbon-neutral claim or market-based adjustment is netted. Main permit 6229374-CN flags emergency systems and renewable-purchase documentation on drawing G005; current permit attachments and fuel-monitoring descriptions expose no generator count/rating, purchase volume or annual sourcing. Exact PSCAA/Ecology searches returned no public SE3 order, registration or emissions series. No electricity/water volume, bill, demand, rate code, PUE/WUE, generator inventory/runtime, fuel, renewable share, measured emissions or discharge series was found.

source.title: Equinix 2011 Form 10-Q, Exhibit 10.2 — 2020 Fifth Avenue Lease
source.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Equinix
source.notes: The executed lease names 2020 Fifth Avenue LLC as landlord and Switch & Data WA One LLC, a wholly owned Equinix subsidiary, as tenant. It covers data-center levels five through eight intended to contain approximately 51,000 square feet for an initial 180-month term, allocates 9 MW from two Seattle City Light basement vaults with actual draw not to exceed 4.5 MW from either vault, and requires the landlord to pay City Light and rebill submetered tenant amounts. It also requires monthly Additional Rent with annual reconciliation, including 100% of real-property taxes and broad general or special assessments minus a parking-garage allocation, and 50% of the annual City skybridge fee. PDF pages 101-102 / printed lease pages 16-17 were rendered and visually inspected for the tax and fee formulas; PDF page 105 / printed lease page 20 was rendered for the electrical allocation. The current tenant tax amount cannot be reconstructed without the landlord's annual reconciliation, current 2020 garage-space count and replacement comparable-garage tax rate. The power allocation was prospective at execution and is not a commissioning record, meter observation, bill, or utility expense.

research_updates.notes: Sources searched: Equinix Foundation and social-impact pages, historical 2014 Impact Grant announcement, SEC/IRS nonprofit-filing routes, Seattle and King County agendas, school/workforce organizations, nonprofit recipient pages and local reporting. Searches combined Equinix Seattle, SE3, 2020 Fifth, King County, donation, grant, sponsorship, scholarship, school, workforce, apprenticeship, training, nonprofit, volunteer, 990 and recipient across 2013-2026. The 2014 program offered grants up to $25,000 to named global/national organizations, while the Equinix Foundation began in 2022; neither source or a recipient filing identifies an SE3-funded amount. Companywide grants, matching gifts and volunteer hours are not allocated. No recipient-confirmed project cash or in-kind amount, training payment, apprenticeship funding, school contribution or SE3 community ledger was found.

research_updates.title: County-outcome audit — observable industry growth is not an SE3 effect
research_updates.notes: The official Census County Business Patterns county files were queried for King County 53033 and NAICS 518210 in pre-opening 2012 and latest available 2023. The returned aggregates move from 9,269 employees, 266 establishments and $1.043425 billion annual payroll to 12,670 employees, 277 establishments and $2.72945 billion. They cover the county's many hosting, cloud and data-processing firms, other Equinix facilities including pre-existing SE2 and later SE4, and concurrent regional technology growth. No treatment share, unaffected comparator, parallel-trends diagnostic, event isolation, project employment series or defensible counterfactual exists. County employment: reject; county payroll/wages: reject; county GDP: reject.

source.title: County Business Patterns 2023 — County File
source.notes: The official 2012 and 2023 county files were queried for Washington state 53, King County 033 and NAICS 518210. They return 9,269 employees, 266 establishments and $1,043,425 thousand annual payroll in 2012, versus 12,670 employees, 277 establishments and $2,729,450 thousand payroll in 2023. These county-industry aggregates encompass many employers and facilities and cannot isolate SE3 or supply a causal comparison.

research_updates.notes: Directed third-pass sources included Seattle Council/Clerk files, Waterfront LID rolls, King assessor/tax pages, Seattle permit archives, SEC 8-K/10-Q/10-K exhibits, Digital Realty acquisition disclosures, operator archives and web searches. Exact identifiers were Equinix, Switch & Data WA One LLC, 2020 Fifth Avenue LLC, 2020 Fifth Holdings LLC, SE3, 2020 5TH AVE, parcel 0659000905, permits 6229374/6262351/3010224 and lease, deed, lien, UCC, bond, loan, financing, litigation, penalty, settlement and compliance across 2010-2026. The records establish a 15-year build-to-suit lease, landlord parcel, LID assessment and financing-lease accounting context but no project public loan, bond, developer cash ledger, deed consideration tied to SE3, paid penalty, litigation recovery, tax appeal outcome or equipment financing balance.

source.title: Waterfront Seattle Final Assessment Roll
source.notes: The final roll identifies parcel 0659000905 as PARKING GARAGE / DATA CENTER, taxpayer 2020 Fifth Holdings LLC, and lists $104,000 of special benefit with a $40,749.49 final Waterfront LID assessment. The lease broadly defines tenant-reimbursable real-property taxes to include general and special assessments, net of a garage allocation, so contractual tenant incidence is plausible; however, no landlord reconciliation, replacement garage comparator, payment schedule or tenant invoice establishes the SE3 amount or timing. The assessment is not treated as project construction cost or netted against ad valorem taxes.

research_updates.title: Candidate-by-candidate modeling and acceptance decision
research_updates.notes: Metric-specific review after both direct-evidence passes and directed gap closure. Investment: retain only Digital Realty's approximately $4.1 million funded 50%-JV contribution; reject the $22.9 million commitment, operator plan, rent obligation and accounting basis as actual construction or total-project cash. Construction: retain two separate low-confidence sensitivities—the AGC/DJC $50 million/$75 million/$100 million award-category endpoints and midpoint, and 50,482 hours × $27.38 Seattle wage with 0.75/1.00/1.25 wage-mix factors. The former is not audited spend or an exact cost; the latter is not certified payroll, compensation, local earnings or headcount. Suppliers: reject the tested non-labor residual because category-cost coverage and worker-hour completeness are definitionally incompatible; names also lack payments and geography. Operations: retain a strictly conditional one-active-security-post 24x7 floor of 4.2115/4.8433/5.4750 FTE-equivalents and $150,496.80/$229,586.46/$259,532.52 annual base-wage benchmark using official relief factors and regional wages; these are not observed posts, headcount, staffing, payroll or vendor expense. Fiscal/public costs: retain the $391,063.45 same-account break-even identity, not a tenant amount or net benefit; lease tax and fee formulas lack the annual reconciliation and comparator. Resources: retain the 25/50/100-percent 9-MW utilization sensitivity and add conditional $833,733/$2,605,662/$10,777,428 energy-charge/retail-price benchmarks and 5,679.48/11,358.96/22,717.92 metric-ton NWPP location-based emissions sensitivities. They are not consumption observations, bills, tariff assignments, measured emissions or market-based Scope 2 results. Community and causal county outcomes remain rejected. No input-output multiplier, arbitrary lease/building allocation, tax-rate multiplication or causal effect is introduced.

project_description: Equinix SE3 is an operating colocation facility at 2020 Fifth Avenue in Seattle, King County, Washington, opened March 14, 2013 after conversion and vertical expansion of a 1975 parking garage. This account follows Equinix's four-level leasehold and current 36,457-square-foot colocation offering within parcel 0659000905; it does not treat the landlord's wider building and garage or nearby Equinix SE2 in the Westin Building as the same facility.
